after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the secant-tangent identity:

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta 
$$

We rewrite the given expression using the secant-tangent identity as follows:

$$
\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{sec}⁡\theta }{1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }=\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{sec}⁡\theta }{{sec}^{2}⁡\theta }
$$

We now simplify the expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{sec}⁡\theta }{{sec}^{2}⁡\theta } & =\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{sec}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{sec}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \cdot \cancel{\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta }}{\cancel{\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta }\cdot \operatorname{sec}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we recall the following identities:

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta },\,\frac{1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta }=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta 
$$

 

Using the above identities, we can further simplify our expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta } & =\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }}\cdot \cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{sec}⁡\theta }{1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$
